title: fix(search): surface per-source fallback outcomes in people search (#3804)
body:
## Description

People search degraded silently. When NIP-50 relays timed out or the
Funnelcake REST API was unavailable, `UserSearchBloc` collapsed the
result into either `success` (with whatever accumulated) or `failure`,
and `PeopleSection` rendered "No results found for X" — visually
identical to a true miss. The lived consequence is #3791: users typed
a friend's username, saw an empty results screen, and concluded the
friend wasn't on Divine.

This PR threads per-source provenance from the repository all the way
to the UI:

- `ProfileRepository.searchUsersProgressive` now emits
  `Stream<ProgressiveSearchResult>` carrying both the profile list and
  a `Map<SearchSource, SearchSourceStatus>` recording each phase's
  outcome (success / failed / skipped, with latency and a typed
  failure reason).
- `UserSearchBloc` mirrors the map in state, promotes pending sources
  to `failed(timeout)` when the outer 20 s stream timeout fires, and
  exposes an `isDegradedEmpty` getter (`results.isEmpty AND any source
  failed`).
- `PeopleSection` routes degraded-empty to the existing
  `SearchSectionErrorState` (with Try-again button), instead of the
  misleading "No results found".
- Per-source latency / failure flows into a new
  `FeedPerformanceTracker.trackSearchSource` event so we can answer
  in the field whether NIP-50, Funnelcake, or the query itself is the
  culprit.
- New canonical contract doc at `mobile/docs/PEOPLE_SEARCH.md`
  (partial payment of #3627, the data-source-strategy doc gap from
  the parent epic).

The 5 s NIP-50 timeout is also lifted to a file-local constant for
symmetry with the other timeouts in `profile_repository.dart`, and
the bloc's outer 20 s timeout is lifted to
`search_constants.userSearchOuterTimeout`.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3791. Closes #3804. Refs #3801 (parent
epic), #3627 (data-source doc — partial), #3593 (suppressed catch
blocks — partial, Phase 3 of progressive search).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] 📝 Documentation

## How Has This Been Tested?

From `mobile/`:
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- `flutter test test/blocs/user_search/` — 44 tests, all green
  (8 new: source-provenance group + tracker round-trip + outer-
  timeout-marks-pending + four `isDegradedEmpty` getter cases;
  existing tests migrated to envelope shape).
- `flutter test test/screens/search_results/widgets/people_section_test.dart`
  — 15 tests, all green (4 new degraded-empty cases).
- `flutter test test/services/feed_performance_tracker_test.dart` — 4
  tests, all green (1 new: `trackSearchSource` smoke test).
- `flutter test test/widgets/find_people_sheet_test.dart
  test/widgets/user_picker_sheet_test.dart` — 30 tests, all green
  (mechanical stub migration only — these features aren't part of
  #3804's UX work).
- `(cd packages/profile_repository && flutter test)` — 212 tests, all
  green (5 new in `source provenance` sub-group, existing progressive
  tests migrated to the `.profiles` accessor on the envelope).

Manual verification will be added once a TestFlight build is cut.

## Out of scope (per parent-epic decomposition)

- Auto-navigate-while-typing (#3802)
- Focus / keyboard continuity (#3803, #3020)
- Blocklist filtering of search (#3805, #948)
- Changing the 5 s NIP-50 timeout value (parent epic Q3)
- Replacing or extending the NIP-50 relay list (parent epic Q4)
- Replacing the non-progressive sibling `searchUsers` (used by
  `NewMessageSearchBloc` — different scope)
- Whole-bloc `addError` sweep (#3592)

title: search: improve timeout / fallback UX for people search
body:
## Summary

People search can degrade under NIP-50 timeout fallback, making search feel unreliable and contributing to the perception that the search flow is hanging.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about **people search reliability and fallback UX**.

Confirmed:
- `ProfileRepository.searchUsersProgressive` can hit NIP-50 timeout fallback.
- Users report not being able to find expected accounts.
- Search route transitions can happen before the user understands whether results are loading, partial, or failed.

Related issue:
- #3791 — cant find friends

## Confirmed facts

From reproduction logs:
- Search route pushes successfully.
- NIP-50 search can timeout after 5 seconds.
- Cache/indexer enrichment can still happen afterward.

## Problem

The current people-search behavior mixes remote timeout, fallback, and eventual enrichment without a clearly defined user experience. This makes search quality feel random.

## Questions to resolve

- What is the canonical fallback order for people search?
- What should the UI show during relay timeout, fallback, and partial results?
- What instrumentation do we need to understand failure modes in the field?

## Acceptance criteria

- The data-source strategy for people search is explicit.
- Timeout and fallback behavior are instrumented and understandable.
- The UI communicates partial/slow/fallback states intentionally.
- #3791 has a clear execution path under this issue.



---

## Assignee
`@realmeylisdev`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Sequencing
- Start after entry/focus behavior is no longer moving.
- Can run in parallel with filtering work.

## Parent
- `#3801`

## Dependencies
- Prefer after `#3803` is resolved.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this child issue as the execution source of truth for people-search fallback UX
- read `#3801` before implementation

## Engineering Standard
Fix the problem without adding new technical debt. If the touched path already has known audit or refactor debt, repay the relevant portion as part of the implementation instead of layering on a narrow patch.

### Summary

----------------------------------------------

Divine User, May 5, 2026, 13:36

Significant System Latency and UI Lag

The entire application interface is experiencing heavy lagging. Touch inputs are delayed, transitions between screens are stuttering, and overall responsiveness has dropped significantly, making the app difficult to navigate.

App Version: 1.0.9+532

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open the application.
2. Attempt to scroll through any list or navigate between different tabs.
3. Observe the delay between a physical touch gesture and the on-screen reaction.
4. Note the stuttering animations during screen transitions.

### Expected Behavior
The UI should remain fluid and responsive. Transitions should be smooth, and touch inputs should register immediately without any noticeable lag or frame drops.

title: feat(video-player): implement the native video-player in the feed
body:
## Description This PR extends #2731 and implements the native `DivineVideoPlayer` package in the home/explore feed. It replaces the feed-player path there, but it does not remove `media_kit` from every remaining playback surface in the app. The following will be improved in the feed-player path: - No preloading limitation beyond the configured window size - Rewritten structure that removes duplication and makes follow-on migration simpler - HLS playback support in the Android feed path - No more thumbnail fallback when swiping, which improves perceived playback continuity - Smaller bundle size in this path because ffmpeg is no longer needed here - Hot restart no longer crashes in the migrated feed path - New scroll physics closer to TikTok/Instagram feel ### Video cache & download pipeline - **Cancellable prefetch downloads.** Replaced `flutter_cache_manager`'s prefetch download path with a custom `CancellableDownloader` so cancelled prefetches stop consuming bandwidth promptly instead of running to completion in the background. - **Platform-native HTTP preference for the cancellable media-cache path.** - **iOS:** `cupertino_http` via `NSURLSession` - **Android:** `cronet_http` via Chromium net stack - **Desktop / fallback:** `dart:io HttpClient` - Fallback remains in place so devices without the preferred native stack still keep a working downloader. - **Cache files survive app restart.** The cancellable download path persists via `store.putFile(CacheObject(...))` so cached videos remain reachable on next launch. - **Alias map for fallback URLs.** When a video is cached under a fallback key, the manifest also registers it under the stable `aliasKey`, persisted across launches, so the prefetcher does not retry the failing first-attempt URL after a cold start. ## Example Video-Format HLS on Android

title: Complete divine_video_player migration

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Dependency updates, vendored overrides, and storage consolidation

body:
**Problem**: Video playback currently uses a forked `media_kit` (wrapping libmpv/ffmpeg). While the team controls the fork, the underlying stack adds bundle size (ffmpeg) and introduces an abstraction layer between the app and the native platform players. Work is already underway (PR #3242) to replace it with `divine_video_player`, which uses platform APIs directly (ExoPlayer on Android, AVPlayer on iOS/macOS).

**Evidence**: `divine_video_player` already exists in `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/` (~1,000 lines of Dart, plus native platform code). `pooled_video_player` (current player, 21 Dart files) wraps the `media_kit` fork. PR #3242 integrates `divine_video_player` into the feed behind an experimental feature flag. The new player resolves several concrete issues: HLS support on Android, smoother swiping (no thumbnail fallback), higher preload limits, smaller bundle size (no ffmpeg), and hot restart stability.

**Trade-off**: Maintaining a custom video player built on native APIs is a significant long-term commitment: platform API changes, codec edge cases, and device-specific bugs become the team's responsibility. However, video playback is the core of diVine. Using native APIs directly removes the libmpv/ffmpeg layer, reduces bundle size, and gives the team a simpler stack to reason about and debug.

**Impact**: High. Directly affects the core user experience (feed scrolling, playback quality, format support).

**Effort**: High. The player package exists and is being integrated. Remaining work: complete feed integration, migrate all other playback surfaces (explore, profile, video detail, editor preview), remove `media_kit`/`pooled_video_player`, and establish test coverage for the new package.

**Related**: #2732

**Source**: [Code Review — Dependencies](docs/code-review/issues-dependencies.md)

title: ci: Cloudflare API token rejected on PR preview + web prod deploys (auth error 9109)
body:
The Cloudflare API token used by our deploy workflows is being rejected by the Cloudflare API.

## Failing run
https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/actions/runs/25679919012 (PR #4253 preview deploy)

## Errors

\`\`\`
ERROR  A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/***/pages/projects/openvine-app) failed.
  Authentication error [code: 10000]

ERROR  A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts) failed.
  Invalid access token [code: 9109]
\`\`\`

Both \`apiToken\` and \`accountId\` secrets resolved (wrangler-action's \`with:\` block showed them populated), so the token reached Cloudflare and was rejected at auth — not a missing-secret problem. The double rejection (account-scoped \`10000\` then global \`/accounts\` \`9109\`) is Cloudflare's "this token can't authenticate at all" pattern, not a per-resource permissions issue.

Most likely the \`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN\` repo secret has been revoked, expired, or rotated out of Cloudflare since the last successful run.

## Scope

The same secret powers two workflows:

- \`.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_deploy.yml\` — PR previews (currently broken)
- \`.github/workflows/mobile_web_production_deploy.yml\` — production web deploys (will fail next run)

So this is not just a per-PR annoyance — the next prod web deploy fires with the same broken token.

## Fix

1. In Cloudflare → My Profile → API Tokens, rotate the token with \`Cloudflare Pages: Edit\` permission scoped to the \`openvine-app\` project.
2. In divinevideo/divine-mobile → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions, update \`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN\`. Verify \`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID\` is still current while you're there.
3. Re-run the failed workflow on PR #4253 to confirm.

## Unrelated note

The same run surfaced a Node.js 20 deprecation warning for \`actions/checkout@v4\`, \`actions/download-artifact@v5\`, \`actions/github-script@v7\`, and \`cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3\`. Node 20 is removed from runners 2026-09-16. Worth bumping when convenient — not blocking this fix.
